title: From Worse to Victory! Art of the Comeback!! | Caro-Kann: Fantasy | GM Naroditsky’s Theory Speed Run

moves.spoken: We take White and face the Caro-Kann.
We build the centre with d4.
Black challenges with d5.

We play f3 — the Fantasy Variation. It's the kryptonite of most Caro-Kann players: less studied than the mainline trifecta, and so sharp that Black can't get away with just improvising standard Caro moves.
Black takes on e4.
We recapture on e4, and Black plays ...e5, the main line. Note we must not grab with our own pawn on e5 — ...Qh4 with check would then pick off the e4-pawn — so we prioritise development.
We develop the knight to f3.
Black pins with the bishop to g4, the best move.

Against ...Bg4 there are two roads: the solid c3 then bishop to e2 that I play, and the more ambitious bishop to c4 I recommend for stronger players — it forces Black to demonstrate deep theory and sets countless tactical traps.
We bring the bishop to c4. In past games the shot on f7 has been overlooked by unprepared opponents.
Black correctly plays the knight to d7, guarding against the f7 sacrifice.
We castle kingside — a big appeal of the Fantasy: the semi-open f-file that fuels the attack.
Black develops the knight to f6. Now we must shore up the centre, because once Black is developed ...exd4 grows nasty.
We play c3 to buttress the centre — the b1-knight can develop via d2 later. And a capture on e5 doesn't work: Black would take our f3-knight first, and then the centre just evaporates.
Black develops the bishop to d6. As a rule, get the bishop out before the knight, so one piece doesn't block another.
We develop the bishop to g5, its one good square.
Black plays ...h6, and this is about where most club players leave theory.
We retreat to h4, provoking ...g5.
Black plays ...g5.
We drop the bishop to g3 — and remember, ...Nxe4 is never a real problem, because the check on f7 always answers it.

Black plays the queen to e7, solidifying e5 and preparing to castle queenside — an opposite-wing race, with Black storming ...h5–h4 while we can advance a4–a5 or swing the queen to b3 or a4 to worry his weak queenside pawns.
First we complete development with the knight to d2.

Black castles queenside. Before pawn-storming, apply the best-case-scenario test: even if a4–a5–a6 all worked, Black just plays ...b5 and we've wasted three tempi for an unexploitable weakness — so we attack with pieces instead, starting with the queen to a4, and don't forget the standing weakness on f7.
